text.p: Italian bond futures slumped back by late afternoon as the weak lira, EMU issues and political concerns over how determined the government was to rein in its budget deficit returned to haunt the BTP market, dealers said.
The market had started slightly firmed reflecting lower than expected growth in Italian producer prices for December, but then sellers emerged as the worries returned.

Dealers said that investors were concerned that Italy would not be able to join the European single currency in the first round after a reported remark by Belgian central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse, later denied, over Italy and the EMU.

Verplaetse denied he made comments in the newspaper that EMU would best start without Italy since the country will not be able to meet EMU entry criteria on budget deficits. But market nerves had been rattled and the damage done.
"The market was fragile and just waiting for some bad news as an excuse to sell, the lira clearly suffer a bout of nerves," said one LIFFE trader.

The lira was also undermined by the weakness in the dollar after the U.S. currency hit a high of 1.70 per mark early. While most other world bond markets were weaker, with only German bunds holding to positive territory.

Dealers said that market will start to look towards preliminary Italy CPI figures for February on Thursday and Friday for 11 Italian cities with analysts expecting annual 2.5 percent after 2.6 percent in January.
